title: VLAN Trunk Native VLAN Mismatch
symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot communicate with PC2 in VLAN 10 across Switch-A and Switch-B. CDP logs Native VLAN mismatch warnings.
topology_note: PC1 (192.168.10.10/24) on Switch-A Fa0/1 (VLAN 10). Switch-A G0/1 to Switch-B G0/1 Trunk. Switch-B Fa0/1 (VLAN 10) to PC2 (192.168.10.20/24).
show_outputs:
Switch-A# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gig0/1      on               802.1q         trunking      1

Switch-B# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gig0/1      on               802.1q         trunking      99

Switch-A# show logging
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (1), with Switch-B GigabitEthernet0/1 (99).
expected_fault: Trunk native VLAN mismatch between Switch-A (Native VLAN 1) and Switch-B (Native VLAN 99).
recommended_fix_steps:
Switch-A(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1
Switch-A(config-if)# switchport trunk native vlan 99
verification_command: Switch-A# show interfaces trunk | include Native vlan

title: Access VLAN Not Defined in VLAN Database
symptom: Accounting PC connected to Switch-1 Fa0/5 cannot ping its default gateway 192.168.20.1. Port LED stays amber.
topology_note: PC (192.168.20.50/24) -> Switch-1 Fa0/5 (Access VLAN 20) -> Router-1 subinterface G0/0.20.
show_outputs:
Switch-1# show interfaces FastEthernet0/5 switchport
Name: Fa0/5
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (inactive)

Switch-1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4
10   Sales                            active    Fa0/6, Fa0/7
99   Management                       active    Fa0/24
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is assigned to Fa0/5 but does not exist in the switch VLAN database (status inactive).
recommended_fix_steps:
Switch-1(config)# vlan 20
Switch-1(config-vlan)# name Accounting
Switch-1(config-vlan)# exit

title: Router-on-a-Stick Dot1Q Encapsulation Mismatch
symptom: Host in VLAN 30 (192.168.30.5) cannot reach its default gateway (192.168.30.1) or other VLANs.
topology_note: Host (192.168.30.5) in VLAN 30 on Switch-1 -> Trunk link to Router-1 G0/0. Router-1 uses subinterfaces for inter-VLAN routing.
show_outputs:
Router-1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 300
 ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0

Switch-1# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gig0/1      on               802.1q         trunking      1
Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gig0/1      1-4094
expected_fault: Router-1 subinterface G0/0.30 is tagged with encapsulation dot1Q 300 instead of dot1Q 30.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
Router-1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 30
Router-1(config-subif)# ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0

title: VLAN Pruned from Trunk Allowed List
symptom: Engineering department (VLAN 40) users on Switch-2 cannot ping file server on Switch-1. VLAN 10 and 20 work normally.
topology_note: Switch-1 (Core) <---> Switch-2 (Access) via G0/2 trunk link. Server in VLAN 40 on Switch-1; PCs in VLAN 40 on Switch-2.
show_outputs:
Switch-2# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gig0/2      on               802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gig0/2      10,20,99

Port        Vlans in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned
Gig0/2      10,20,99
expected_fault: VLAN 40 is omitted from the switchport trunk allowed vlan list on interface Gig0/2.
recommended_fix_steps:
Switch-2(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/2
Switch-2(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40

title: Trunk Port Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) Negotiation Failure
symptom: Switch-A and Switch-B link is connected, but traffic across VLANs fails. Link behaves as an access link on VLAN 1.
topology_note: Switch-A Fa0/24 connected to Switch-B Fa0/24. Both switches configured with dynamic auto.
show_outputs:
Switch-A# show interfaces FastEthernet0/24 switchport
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: static access
Administrative Trunking Encapsulation: dot1q
Operational Trunking Encapsulation: native
Negotiation of Trunking: On

Switch-B# show interfaces FastEthernet0/24 switchport
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: static access
Administrative Trunking Encapsulation: dot1q
Operational Trunking Encapsulation: native
Negotiation of Trunking: On
expected_fault: Both ends of the link are set to dynamic auto, so neither end initiates trunk negotiation, defaulting to access mode.
recommended_fix_steps:
Switch-A(config)# interface FastEthernet0/24
Switch-A(config-if)# switchport mode trunk

Switch-B(config)# interface FastEthernet0/24
Switch-B(config-if)# switchport mode trunk

IP Address......................: 192.168.1.15
Subnet Mask.....................: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway.................: 192.168.1.254
DNS Servers.....................: 8.8.8.8

Router-1# show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0     192.168.1.1     YES manual up                    up      
GigabitEthernet0/1     203.0.113.2     YES manual up                    up

title: HSRP Virtual IP and Group Mismatch
symptom: Host default gateway 10.1.1.1 fluctuates between Router-1 and Router-2, causing packet loss and duplicate ARP warnings.
topology_note: Router-1 (Primary) and Router-2 (Standby) providing default gateway redundancy for 10.1.1.0/24 LAN via HSRP.
show_outputs:
Router-1# show standby brief
                     P Indicates configured to preempt.
                     |
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gig0/0      10   110 P Active  local           unknown         10.1.1.1

Router-2# show standby brief
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gig0/0      20   100   Active  local           unknown         10.1.1.254
expected_fault: HSRP group mismatch: Router-1 is in HSRP group 10 (Virtual IP 10.1.1.1) while Router-2 is in group 20 (Virtual IP 10.1.1.254), resulting in dual active routers and no standby pairing.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-2(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0
Router-2(config-if)# no standby 20
Router-2(config-if)# standby 10 ip 10.1.1.1
Router-2(config-if)# standby 10 priority 100

title: Switch Management IP Default Gateway Missing
symptom: Network Administrator in subnet 10.200.1.0/24 cannot SSH or ping Switch-3 on VLAN 99 IP (10.99.1.10). Local ping within 10.99.1.0/24 works.
topology_note: Switch-3 has SVI interface VLAN 99 (10.99.1.10/24). Gateway router is 10.99.1.1.
show_outputs:
Switch-3# show running-config | include default-gateway
(No output returned)

Switch-3# show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
Vlan99                 10.99.1.10      YES manual up                    up      
FastEthernet0/1        unassigned      YES unset  up                    up
expected_fault: Switch-3 is missing the 'ip default-gateway 10.99.1.1' configuration, making it unable to reply to management traffic from remote subnets.
recommended_fix_steps: Switch-3(config)# ip default-gateway 10.99.1.1
verification_command: Switch-3# show running-config | include ip default-gateway

title: Subnet Mask Mismatch on Point-to-Point Link
symptom: Router-A cannot ping Router-B across the WAN link. OSPF adjacency is stuck in INIT/DOWN.
topology_note: Router-A G0/0/0 connected to Router-B G0/0/0 with subnet 172.16.0.0.
show_outputs:
Router-A# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet address is 172.16.0.1/30
  Broadcast address is 172.16.0.3

Router-B# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet address is 172.16.0.2/24
  Broadcast address is 172.16.0.255

recommended_fix_steps:

Router-B(config-if)# ip address 172.16.0.2 255.255.255.252
verification_command: Router-B# show ip interface brief GigabitEthernet0/0/0

show_outputs:
Router-1# show ip dhcp pool FLOOR2
Pool FLOOR2 :

 Subnet size (total/usable)     : 16/14

 Pending event                  : none

Router-1# show ip dhcp binding
IP address       Client-ID/Hardware address     Lease expiration        Type
192.168.2.2      0001.6421.33A1                 Infinite                Automatic

title: Missing DHCP Excluded Addresses Causing Gateway IP Conflict
symptom: Users intermittently lose internet access. Router console throws %IP-4-DUP_ADDR: Duplicate address 192.168.1.1 on GigabitEthernet0/0.
topology_note: Router-1 G0/0 IP: 192.168.1.1/24. DHCP pool assigns 192.168.1.0/24.
show_outputs:
Router-1# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
 network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.1.1
 dns-server 8.8.8.8

Router-1# show ip dhcp binding
IP address       Client-ID/Hardware address     Lease expiration        Type
192.168.1.1      0050.7966.6801                 Infinite                Automatic
192.168.1.2      0050.7966.6802                 Infinite                Automatic
expected_fault: DHCP server leased the router's own IP address (192.168.1.1) to a host because no 'ip dhcp excluded-address' was configured.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-1(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.10
Router-1# clear ip dhcp binding *
verification_command: Router-1# show running-config | include ip dhcp excluded-address

title: OSPF Area ID Mismatch on Point-to-Point Link
symptom: Router-1 and Router-2 are directly connected via GigabitEthernet0/0/0, but OSPF neighbor adjacency is never formed.
topology_note: Link subnet 10.0.12.0/30. Router-1 (ID 1.1.1.1), Router-2 (ID 2.2.2.2).
show_outputs:
Router-1# show ip ospf neighbor
(Empty output - no neighbors)

Router-1# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.0.12.1/30, Area 0
  Process ID 1, Router ID 1.1.1.1, Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1

Router-2# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.0.12.2/30, Area 1
  Process ID 1, Router ID 2.2.2.2, Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1
expected_fault: OSPF Area ID mismatch: Router-1 interface is in Area 0 while Router-2 interface is in Area 1.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-2(config)# router ospf 1
Router-2(config-router)# no network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 1
Router-2(config-router)# network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0

title: OSPF Inverted Wildcard Mask in Network Statement
symptom: Router-HQ does not advertise subnet 192.168.100.0/24 into OSPF. Downstream routers cannot reach HQ server LAN.
topology_note: HQ LAN is 192.168.100.0/24 on G0/1. OSPF Process 10 running.
show_outputs:
Router-HQ# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 10
 router-id 10.10.10.10
 network 192.168.100.0 255.255.255.0 area 0

Router-HQ# show ip ospf interface brief
Interface    PID   Area            IP Address/Mask    Cost  State Nbrs F/C
Gi0/0        10    0               10.1.1.1/30        1     P2P   1/1
(Gi0/1 is missing from OSPF enabled interfaces)
expected_fault: OSPF network command used subnet mask 255.255.255.0 instead of wildcard mask 0.0.0.255, failing to match interface Gi0/1.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-HQ(config)# router ospf 10
Router-HQ(config-router)# no network 192.168.100.0 255.255.255.0 area 0

verification_command: Router-HQ# show ip ospf interface brief

title: OSPF Hello and Dead Timer Mismatch
symptom: OSPF neighbor state between R1 and R2 stays in DOWN or cycles continuously with %OSPF-5-ADJCHG warnings.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected on WAN link 10.10.10.0/30.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip ospf interface Serial0/0/0
Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.10.10.1/30, Area 0
  Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40, Wait 40, Retransmit 5

R2# show ip ospf interface Serial0/0/0
Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.10.10.2/30, Area 0
  Timer intervals configured, Hello 5, Dead 20, Wait 20, Retransmit 5
expected_fault: OSPF Hello/Dead timer mismatch: R1 is using 10/40 seconds while R2 is using 5/20 seconds.
recommended_fix_steps:
R2(config)# interface Serial0/0/0
R2(config-if)# ip ospf hello-interval 10
R2(config-if)# ip ospf dead-interval 40

title: OSPF Passive-Interface Misconfigured on Routing Link
symptom: Branch router R-BR1 fails to form OSPF adjacency with Core router R-CORE across link G0/0.
topology_note: R-BR1 G0/0 connects to R-CORE G0/0. R-BR1 G0/1 connects to User LAN.
show_outputs:
R-BR1# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
 network 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0

R-BR1# show ip ospf neighbor
(Empty)
expected_fault: Interface GigabitEthernet0/0 (the transit link to R-CORE) is configured as passive-interface, suppressing OSPF Hellos.
recommended_fix_steps:
R-BR1(config)# router ospf 1
R-BR1(config-router)# no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0

title: RIPv2 Auto-Summary Discontiguous Subnet Drop
symptom: Routers running RIPv2 experience erratic routing to 172.16.1.0/24 and 172.16.2.0/24 separated by a 192.168.1.0/24 link.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip protocols
Routing Protocol is "rip"
  Sending updates every 30 seconds
  Automatic network summarization is in effect
  Routing for Networks:
    172.16.0.0
    192.168.1.0

R2# show ip route rip
R    172.16.0.0/16 [120/1] via 192.168.1.1, FastEthernet0/0
                   [120/1] via 192.168.1.6, FastEthernet0/1
expected_fault: RIPv2 automatic summarization is enabled, summarizing discontiguous /24 subnets into a single 172.16.0.0/16 classful route.

R2(config-router)# no auto-summary

R3(config)# router rip
R3(config-router)# no auto-summary

show_outputs:

Standard IP access list 10
    10 deny 192.168.1.50 (20 matches)
    20 permit any (145 matches)

Router-1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 10 in
expected_fault: Standard ACL 10 filters source IP 192.168.1.50 but was applied inbound ('in') on G0/1 (WAN interface), where incoming packets have source IPs in 10.0.0.0/24 or public ranges.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1
Router-1(config-if)# no ip access-group 10 in
Router-1(config-if)# ip access-group 10 out

title: Extended ACL Implicit Deny Blocking Legitimate Web Traffic
symptom: Sales PC (192.168.10.15) cannot browse the intranet web server at 10.1.1.80 on HTTP port 80. Ping to server is blocked.
topology_note: Router-1 G0/0 has inbound ACL 101.
show_outputs:
Router-1# show ip access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
    10 permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.1.1.80 eq 443
    20 permit udp any any eq domain
    (implicit deny ip any any active - 84 matches)

Router-1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 101 in
expected_fault: ACL 101 permits HTTPS (port 443) but lacks a permit statement for HTTP (port 80), hitting the implicit deny.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-1(config)# ip access-list extended 101
Router-1(config-ext-nacl)# 15 permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.1.1.80 eq www

title: ACL Rule Order Shadowing Specific Permit
symptom: Network Manager PC (192.168.10.5) is unable to access the Finance Database (10.50.1.10), even though a permit rule was written for it.
topology_note: Core Router G0/0 inbound ACL 'FILTER_FINANCE'.
show_outputs:
Core-Router# show access-lists FILTER_FINANCE
Extended IP access list FILTER_FINANCE
    10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 10.50.1.0 0.0.0.255 (152 matches)
    20 permit ip host 192.168.10.5 host 10.50.1.10 (0 matches)
    30 permit ip any any (530 matches)
expected_fault: Broad deny rule (line 10) shadows and precedes specific permit rule (line 20), denying Host 192.168.10.5 before line 20 is ever evaluated.
recommended_fix_steps:
Core-Router(config)# ip access-list extended FILTER_FINANCE
Core-Router(config-ext-nacl)# no 10
Core-Router(config-ext-nacl)# no 20
Core-Router(config-ext-nacl)# 10 permit ip host 192.168.10.5 host 10.50.1.10
Core-Router(config-ext-nacl)# 20 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 10.50.1.0 0.0.0.255

title: Inverted Wildcard Mask in Extended ACL
symptom: Security rule designed to block entire subnet 192.168.20.0/24 from accessing Server only blocks host 192.168.20.0, allowing other hosts through.
topology_note: Router-1 ACL 110 applied on G0/1 out.
show_outputs:
Router-1# show ip access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
    10 deny ip 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 host 10.0.0.5
    20 permit ip any any (241 matches)
expected_fault: ACL 110 line 10 uses subnet mask '255.255.255.0' instead of wildcard mask '0.0.0.255'.
recommended_fix_steps:
Router-1(config)# ip access-list extended 110
Router-1(config-ext-nacl)# no 10
Router-1(config-ext-nacl)# 10 deny ip 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.5
